sentence: This project studies how myoblast fusion works during skeletal muscle development and muscle stem cell regeneration.
This project tries to find out which genes cause insulin resistance, using single cell methods and mouse models.
This project studies how the liver controls proteins that move drugs and nutrients from the bloodstream into the liver.
This project tests whether delivering a herpes simplex virus gene and a bifunctional antibody into tumors can treat cancer.
This project builds a method that measures the molecular states of individual Salmonella cells during infection.
This project studies why some prosecutors treat an overdose as a murder and how those charges affect the health of people at risk.
This project builds genome editing tools to understand ticks and their pathogen interactions at the molecular level.
This project builds machine learning methods that analyze medical images to make diagnosis more accurate.
This project studies how genomic instability during development causes inflammation in the placenta and embryonic lethality that mostly affects female embryos.
This project tests whether agents that block a nuclear receptor can slow colon cancer growth, using cell culture and mouse tumor models.
This project uses mathematical modeling, machine learning and single-cell genomics to predict how mammalian cells change their fate over time and space.
This project works to reduce infections and blockage in ventricular shunts that drain cerebrospinal fluid in patients with hydrocephalus.
This project uses deep learning on bone marrow tissue samples to link morphology to molecular features in multiple myeloma.
This project applies data science methods to addiction research.
This project studies brain tissue to understand Alzheimer's disease and the effects of repetitive head impacts, using digital pathology and machine learning.
This project uses electroencephalogram-based neuroimaging to find biomarkers of dysfunctional brain networks in patients with chronic low back pain over time.
This project uses artificial intelligence to predict clinical outcomes of psychosis from electronic health records and genetic information.
This project studies how skin regenerates when skin allografts are repopulated, testing a stem cell mobilizing therapy in swine with burns.
This project studies why cancers with isocitrate dehydrogenase mutations become resistant to targeted therapy drugs.
This project builds faster simulations of the musculoskeletal system and uses machine learning to predict how people respond to exoskeletons and powered prostheses.
